caption: Unified leaderboard on the identical 10 outer folds, sorted by mean macro-F1 at test level (mean ± SD over folds); sample-level macro-F1 is secondary.

Family-level contrasts: fold-wise mean macro-F1 of a family of models, paired by outer fold; Wilcoxon and Nadeau–Bengio tests, Holm-corrected over the 3 contrasts. The minimum detectable difference is the smallest mean difference that the Nadeau–Bengio test could call significant given the observed fold-to-fold variability.

Best CNN-based model and best fine-tuned model against the reference (best classical model), paired by outer fold. The 95 % interval and the minimum detectable difference show what this design can and cannot resolve.
Effect of fine-tuning: each backbone fine-tuned vs the same backbone frozen (same folds), Holm-corrected over the backbones.
Effect of ImageNet pre-training: each pretrained fine-tuned backbone vs the small CNN trained from scratch (same folds), Holm-corrected.

Pre-specified decision rule: every CNN-based model against the reference (SVM (RBF)); Holm-corrected over 9 contrasts. The CNN replaces the classical pipeline only if at least one CNN is both better on average and significantly better.

Error overlap between the reference classical model and the best CNN-based model (pooled out-of-fold predictions, repeat 1). Exact McNemar p = 0.932 (test level), 0.845 (sample level; descriptive). Cluster-bootstrap 95 % CI of the accuracy difference (CNN − classical): -0.074 … +0.061.
Error overlap by true class (test level, repeat 1).
Error severity (test level, repeat 1): adjacent-class errors vs two-step errors (NORMAL ↔ MACRO), which are the clinically most serious.
Sample-level accuracy (repeat 1) by distance of the laboratory UACR to the nearest class boundary (30 or 300 mg/g, log scale, tertiles of the 100 samples).
